facts.claim: NU7 is active on testnet from height 4,465,026: blocks target 25 seconds, and v4 transactions are invalid.

librustzcash set NU7's mainnet activation height to 3,543,405 on 21 Oct 2026. Mainnet was at height 3,541,302 on 4 Nov 2026, so at 75-second blocks activation is about 44 hours later. Zebra's mainnet readiness tracker (issue 11674) was still open.
replaces: NU7 mainnet activation is not scheduled yet

facts.claim: NU6.3 (Ironwood) activated on mainnet at block 3,428,143 on 28 Jul 2026, and on testnet at height 4,134,000, after a flaw in Orchard's circuit that could have allowed counterfeit ZEC.
Orchard accepts withdrawals only. New shielded funds go to the Ironwood pool.
Ironwood notes go to the Orchard receiver a unified address already carries, so existing u1 and utest1 addresses keep working.
replaces: unified addresses need a new Ironwood receiver

facts.claim: Testnet addresses start utest1 (unified), ztestsapling1 (Sapling) or tm (transparent). Coins on testnet are TAZ and have no value.

zcash-devtool's wallet init gives the account a default address with a transparent receiver. wallet generate-address with no --pool flag makes an address with shielded receivers only, which is the one to hand to payers.
Use testnet.zec.rocks:443 (gRPC over TLS) as the testnet light-wallet server.
zec.rocks:443 serves mainnet light-wallet clients over gRPC with TLS.
The old testnet light-wallet servers lightwalletd.testnet.electriccoin.co and testnet.lightwalletd.com are dead.

Fauzec sends 1 TAZ per address every 24 hours to unified or Sapling addresses, shielded. Its web form has a Cloudflare Turnstile human check. A claim to a shielded-only unified address arrived in the Ironwood pool in transaction cc2d88b8… (version 6, NU7, height 4,581,808) and was spendable after about 10 confirmations.
Noir Wallet's testnet extension gives its own account a daily TAZ allowance; 1 TAZ arrived on 4 Nov 2026. The wallet can't send it on NU7 yet, so it is only useful for receiving.

Valar's faucet (0.125 TAZ per IP address every 24 hours) refused both a unified address and a Sapling address with "the wallet cannot pay this address", and had made no payouts in the previous 24 hours. Failed claims do not use up the daily allowance.
The Jino Labs faucet is paused for NU7.
At the Free Society Hack, post a utest1 address in the mentors chat and a Zcash mentor sends TAZ.

zexplorer.app shows a testnet transaction at /testnet/tx/<txid>, including version-6 NU7 transactions; the hack's agent guide recommends it. testnet.zcashexplorer.app shows them at /transactions/<txid> in a browser, blocks some scripted requests, and misreads Ironwood value: a 1 TAZ transfer into Ironwood showed "Transaction fee 1.00015 TAZ", because it counts the Orchard part of the transaction but not the Ironwood part. Take amounts and fees from the wallet.

zec.rocks runs explorer.testnet.zec.rocks (testnet) and explorer.zec.rocks (mainnet), but on 4 Nov 2026 both accepted connections and then returned HTTP 503 after about 38 seconds. Link to testnet.zcashexplorer.app instead.

zcash-devtool, built from source (commit 0b3436b), creates a testnet wallet, syncs NU7 testnet, reports Ironwood balances and sends shielded Ironwood payments with memos (transaction c00460bf…, mined at height 4,581,860). It is for prototyping, not production. That commit pins librustzcash from 16 Oct 2026, before NU7's mainnet height was set, so rebuild against a newer pin before using it on mainnet.

Noir Wallet's testnet extension receives TAZ and shows Ironwood balances, but on 4 Nov 2026 its sends on NU7 testnet failed with "transaction uses an incorrect consensus branch id": it signs for the upgrade before NU7, and its source has no testnet NU7 height or branch ID. Until that is fixed, pay from zcash-devtool. The SDK offers connect, getBalance, sendTransaction({ to, amount, memo, fundingSource }) and getTransactionHistory.
replaces: Noir Wallet's testnet build can send on NU7 testnet

facts.claim: Thus Spoke Zakura v0.4 runs a disposable local regtest network in Docker with NU7 and Ironwood active, a faucet and on-demand mining. Its API takes pool 'ironwood' and rejects 'orchard'.
replaces: pool: 'orchard' in the Thus Spoke Zakura API

facts.claim: Zingolib has active Ironwood support work, and zshield-mcp reports real testnet payments through zingo-cli.

zkool2's zkool_graphql is a GraphQL wallet server with NU7 and Ironwood support, watch-only accounts from a viewing key, and built-in NEAR Intents and FROST. The hack's agent guide recommends it for backends and payment watchers. Run it with --allow-unauthenticated only on localhost: it then exposes seeds to anyone who can reach the port.
WebZjs (@chainsafe/webzjs-wallet) is not on npm and has no Ironwood support. Building it needs Rust nightly, wasm-pack, just, yarn and a gRPC-web proxy.
@zcash/monitor in ronykris/zcash-sdk wraps WebZjs, so it inherits WebZjs's NU7 problems. Its @zcash/uri package only builds ZIP 321 links.
zecli from crates.io makes Orchard-only addresses, which cannot receive funds. The git version needs a zidecar server, and none is hosted for testnet.
Zallet and zecd have no NU7 release.
ZPay, the x402 facilitator with a spend-limited agent wallet, needs a self-hosted Zinder stack in Docker.
CipherPay is a hosted checkout that watches a merchant's viewing key and calls the merchant's server when a payment arrives. Its testnet is at testnet.cipherpay.app.
Frontier Compute's zcash-mcp is a read-only ZAP1 attestation server, not a wallet.

Under ZIP 317 the conventional fee is the marginal fee times the larger of 2 and the number of logical actions. The marginal fee is 5,000 zatoshis before Revision 2 and 1,000 from Revision 2. Let the wallet or SDK compute it.
Treat a payment as seen, then mined, then confirmed, and wait for more confirmations on larger amounts. At 25-second testnet blocks, 10 confirmations take about 4 minutes.
replaces: a broadcast payment is a finished payment

facts.claim: Give a payment server a viewing key: it can see incoming payments but cannot spend them. Keep the spending key off the server.
Fund payments from shielded balances. Transparent funding can reveal and link the coins it spends.
Memos go only to shielded recipients and hold at most 512 bytes. Put an order token in them, not personal data.
Keep ZEC amounts as decimal strings or integer zatoshis (1 ZEC is 100,000,000 zatoshis), never as floating-point numbers.

Payment links follow ZIP 321: zcash:<address>?amount=<ZEC with up to 8 decimals>&memo=<base64url, no padding>. Memos are only allowed for shielded addresses, and an unknown req- parameter makes the whole link invalid.
